salting.title: Salting the cabbage
items: The Nongsaro (Rural Development Administration) recipe dips the cabbage in about 15% brine, sprinkles coarse salt between the leaves near the stems and salts it for about 8 hours.
Time depends on cabbage size and room temperature. It is ready when the stem bends without snapping.
Flip the cabbages top to bottom once halfway through for even salting.
Rinse two or three times in cold water, then drain cut side down until well drained.
aT's survey assumes about 6kg of coarse salt to salt 20 heads.

paste.title: Making rice paste
items: The Nongsaro recipe mixes glutinous rice flour and water 1:9 and cooks it while stirring so it doesn't scorch.
Use about 425g of paste per 5kg of salted cabbage. For 20 heads (~44kg salted), that is about 370g of rice flour and 3.4L of water.
Let the paste cool completely before mixing; hot paste can make kimchi sour faster.
Soaking the red pepper flakes in the paste and fish sauce for about 30 minutes gives a better color and an evenly clinging seasoning.

storage.title: Storage
items: Pack kimchi tightly to push out air and cover the top with outer leaves or plastic wrap.
Fill containers only about 80% so juices and gas from fermentation don't overflow.
Kimchi-fridge storage modes are usually set to a low temperature around 0°C. In a regular fridge, use the back of a shelf where temperature is most stable.
Leave kimchi you will eat soon at room temperature for about a day before refrigerating; refrigerate long-keeping kimchi right away.

timing.title: When to make kimjang
items: The Korea Meteorological Administration considers it kimjang time when the daily mean temperature stays at or below 4°C and the daily low at or below 0°C.
Seoul, Gyeonggi, western Gangwon: mid to late November
East and west coasts and southern regions: late November to mid December
South coast: after late December
Warming has pushed the ideal date later. In Seoul it moved from about Nov 25 (1920–1950 average) to about Nov 29 (1981–2010 average).
Government and retailer discounts often concentrate from mid November. Check aT's kimjang cost survey published in November before shopping.

tips.title: Tips to avoid failure
items: Pick cabbages that feel heavy with a full yellow heart, and radishes that are firm and smooth.
Mix two or three heads first, taste, then adjust with fish sauce or salt.
Under-salted cabbage turns bland and watery; over-salted cabbage gets tough and salty.
Oysters and fresh shrimp speed up fermentation and soften kimchi, so leave them out of long-keeping batches.
If you buy pre-salted cabbage, make the seasoning the day before so you can mix as soon as it arrives.

items.q: How much does kimjang for 20 heads of cabbage cost?
items.a: aT's survey released Nov 17, 2026 (as of Nov 16) put kimjang for a family of four (20 heads) at 187,613 KRW, 9.6% lower than mid-November last year (207,634 KRW). This calculator uses the Nov 21, 2024 aT survey (204,315 KRW), the latest with per-item values, as default prices, and you can edit any price to match today's market.

items.q: How many heads are in a 20kg box of pre-salted cabbage?
items.a: It depends on region and cabbage size, but a 20kg box usually holds 8–10 heads. This calculator assumes about 2.2kg per salted head (about 9 heads per 20kg).

items.q: How many heads should a family of four make?
items.a: aT's kimjang survey uses 20 heads for a family of four, about 5 heads per person. Adjust to how much kimchi you eat and how much storage you have.

items.q: Is salting it yourself cheaper than buying pre-salted cabbage?
items.a: Counting only cabbage and salt, salting it yourself is usually cheaper, but salting, rinsing and draining take a day and need large tubs and lots of water. The result panel compares both methods side by side.

items.q: What brine strength and time should I use?
items.a: The Nongsaro (RDA) recipe dips cabbage in about 15% brine and sprinkles coarse salt between the stems, then salts it for about 8 hours. Checking that the stem bends without snapping is more reliable than the clock.

items.q: When is the best time to make kimjang?
items.a: The Korea Meteorological Administration considers it time when the daily mean temperature stays at or below 4°C and the low at or below 0°C. That is usually mid to late November in Seoul and Gyeonggi, late November to mid December in the south, and after late December on the south coast.

items.q: How much rice paste do I need?
items.a: The Nongsaro recipe cooks glutinous rice flour and water at 1:9 and uses about 425g of paste per 5kg of salted cabbage. For 20 heads (~44kg salted), you need about 370g of rice flour.

items.q: How much kimchi do 20 heads make?
items.a: Add the seasoning weight to the salted cabbage weight for a rough figure. For 20 heads, about 44kg of salted cabbage plus about 23kg of seasoning comes to around 67kg, but some water drains while mixing, so the actual amount is a bit less.
